facts.text: Aman Venice occupies the 16th-century Palazzo Papadopoli, one of only eight palazzo monumentali in Venice.
facts.excerpt: taking over all the family’s 16th-century Palazzo Papadopoli (one of only eight palazzo monumentali in Venice)

facts.text: Aman partnered with the Arrivabene family, who still live on the top floors of the palazzo.
facts.excerpt: The Arrivabenes still live in the top floors

facts.text: The Alcova Tiepolo Suite lets guests sleep beneath Giovanni Battista Tiepolo's cherub-filled frescos.
facts.excerpt: Try the Alcova Tiepolo Suite to sleep beneath Giovanni Battista Tiepolo’s cherub-filled frescos

facts.text: The Sansovino Suite has a fireplace by the 16th-century architect Jacopo d'Antonio Sansovino.
facts.excerpt: Or the Sansovino Suite, with its standout fireplace by 16th-century architect Jacopo d'Antonio Sansovino.

facts.text: Guests can arrive by boat from under the Rialto Bridge to the palazzo's private jetty on the Grand Canal.
facts.excerpt: under the Rialto Bridge in a glossy Riva, and up to Palazzo Papadopoli’s private jetty on the Grand Canal.

facts.text: Arva is the hotel's Italian restaurant, with dishes such as Fassona beef carpaccio, rabbit cappelletti pasta and fish stew sourced from the Rialto market.
facts.excerpt: ultra-Italian restaurant Arva—melt-in-the-mouth Fassona beef carpaccio, rabbit cappelletti pasta, and fish stew sourced from the Rialto market.

facts.text: Sunday brunch is served in the gardens beside the Grand Canal, with dishes such as lobster Benedict and hazelnut pancakes.
facts.excerpt: Don’t miss Sunday brunch to feast on lobster Benedict or hazelnut pancakes in the Grand-Canal-side gardens.

facts.text: Arva and The Bar are open to both Aman guests and non-residents.
facts.excerpt: Open to both Aman guests and non-residents

facts.text: The spa has three treatment rooms with ancient beams and offers holistic therapies, some using Aman's natural skincare line.
facts.excerpt: there’s a spa with superb holistic therapies—some using Aman’s new natural skincare line—dispensed in the three ancient-beamed treatment rooms.

facts.text: The hotel is in San Polo, on the other side of the Rialto Bridge from San Marco.
facts.excerpt: Tucked away in San Polo (a.k.a. the other side of the Rialto Bridge from tourist-rammed San Marco)

facts.text: Aman lists the transfer from Marco Polo Airport as 50 minutes by boat.
Each bedroom is set in one of the palazzo's original rooms, so each is unique.
facts.excerpt: all slotted into the palazzo’s original rooms, so each is unique

facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler says the prices are very high.
facts.excerpt: The prices, dear god—they’re enough to sink the city, but what did you expect?
